name: MMAU
ability_definition: The ability to listen to and understand information and ideas presented through spoken words and sentences.

task_realism.reasoning: The speech subset has tasks close to real listening work: retrieving facts from conversations, extracting key highlights, and inferring speaker intent or emotion. But these run on short clips, often drawn from existing datasets. Workplace listening means following meetings, instructions, calls, and lectures over minutes to hours. About two-thirds of the benchmark (environmental sound and music) has no connection to understanding spoken ideas at all.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Inputs are short, pre-segmented clips, and each question is posed after listening. There is no real-time processing, no clarifying questions, no multi-turn follow-up, and no long-context tracking. Real conversational noise and overlapping talk are underrepresented. The noise-substitution check does confirm that models actually use the audio, which helps validity. Still, the conditions are far more controlled and low-stakes than real spoken interaction.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Only about one-third of items test speech, and the headline metric blends speech with sound and music. That dilutes it as a measure of oral comprehension. Within the speech subset, several skills are paralinguistic (stress, emotion, speaker attributes) rather than understanding the content of what was said. Coverage of extended discourse, argument following, and multi-speaker reasoning is thin.

format_match.reasoning: The answer format is forced multiple choice over short audio snippets. Real outputs of listening are notes, summaries, follow-up actions, or conversational responses. MCQ allows elimination strategies and does not require the model to produce the understood content, so it is a fairly artificial format compared with real work artifacts.

transferability_reasoning: MMAU's speech subset does probe real comprehension skills such as conversational fact retrieval and highlight extraction, and it is validated to require audio input. Transfer to workplace oral comprehension is limited by several factors: two-thirds of the benchmark and its headline metric cover non-speech audio, clips are short, the setting is non-interactive, and all answers are multiple choice. Gains on MMAU therefore signal only partial, narrow progress toward understanding real spoken information at work.

2024.metric: accuracy (%) on the MMAU test split, overall average across sound, music and speech domains, multiple-choice
2024.human_reference: Relevant educated adult workforce: typical attentive adult listeners, comparable to the human evaluators used in the MMAU paper.
